stories.title: Uttar Pradesh calls for single-use plastic boycott
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has called for a complete boycott of single-use plastic, citing threats to the environment and human health. He urged citizens to replace the materials with cloth or reusable alternatives. The state government views the current reliance on plastic as a temporary convenience.

stories.title: Study links new plastic chemicals to lower birth weights
stories.summary: A study from NYU Langone Health found that newer plastic chemicals, marketed as safer alternatives to phthalates, are linked to complications during fetal development, including lower birth weight. The industry previously swapped out older, harmful plasticizers for these newer versions. Safety, it seems, is a moving target.

stories.title: Zepto fined for plastic violation in Bengaluru
stories.summary: The Greater Bengaluru Authority imposed a 25,000 rupee fine on Zepto for violating single-use plastic regulations. The penalty followed an enforcement drive conducted by the Chickpete Division health inspector. The company was found to be using prohibited materials during its operations.

stories.title: Balochistan to enforce single-use plastic ban
stories.summary: Balochistan officials announced plans to strictly implement a ban on single-use plastic products and shopping bags across the province. The government intends to combine the enforcement with a new plantation drive to address climate change. Industrial units will be required to comply with the new environmental standards.

stories.title: Delhi raids two unlicensed cosmetic factories
stories.summary: The Delhi government's Drug Control Department raided two unlicensed manufacturing units in Puth Khurd, seizing machinery, raw materials, and finished skincare products. The facilities were operating without valid manufacturing licences. Officials conducted the operation following directives from the Health Minister.

stories.title: Delhi seizes stock from illegal cosmetics units
stories.summary: Delhi drug inspectors raided two unlicensed cosmetics manufacturing units in Pooth Khurd, seizing stock, equipment, and packaging materials. The government is currently testing samples collected from the sites. The crackdown marks an effort to enforce stricter product safety and licensing standards in the capital.

stories.title: Noida police bust counterfeit cigarette operation
stories.summary: Police in Noida arrested two individuals for operating a racket that repackaged and sold counterfeit cigarettes as genuine branded products. Investigators recovered nearly 5,000 empty packs and three packing machines used to rewrap tobacco. The fake products were supplied to small retailers.

stories.title: FSSAI mandates new logo for dairy packaging
stories.summary: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India has directed dairy manufacturers to include a new blue-and-white logo on milk, curd, and paneer packaging. The mandate aims to standardise labelling across the industry. Consumers will soon see the new design on retail shelves.

stories.title: Startup turns chip packets into sunglasses
stories.summary: Material science company Without uses its patented VerdiCycle technology to transform multi-layered plastic packaging into products like sunglasses and deodorant sticks. The company aims to recycle hard-to-process waste while providing employment for waste-picking communities. Plastic packaging is noted for its ability to persist for decades.

The company is currently navigating restructuring talks and remediation efforts related to its operations in Alagoas. Market conditions have shifted since the previous reporting period.

The industry enters 2026 facing volatile feedstock costs and regulatory pressure toward circularity. Supply architectures have become more regionally diversified to manage these ongoing industrial challenges.

stories.title: Traditional plastics market remains resilient
stories.summary: The global market for commodity thermoplastics like polyethylene and polypropylene remains foundational to the industrial economy, according to IndexBox. Growth is supported by packaging and construction demand, particularly in Asia-Pacific. The sector continues to navigate mounting environmental pressure and regulatory requirements.

stories.title: Sachin Tendulkar invests in waste management startup Recykal
stories.summary: Cricket legend Sachin Tendulkar has invested in Recykal, a Hyderabad-based startup, as a strategic investor. The move follows a $23 million bridge funding round closed in June 2026. The company aims to leverage the partnership to drive behavioural change among one billion people regarding waste recovery.

stories.summary: Tendulkar's investment extends the company's recently announced $23 million bridge funding round, which comprised a mix of primary and secondary capital from existing investors and select new family offices. stories.summary: HYDERABAD: Cricket legend Sachin Tendulkar has invested in Hyderabad-based circular economy and waste management technology company Recykal, acquiring an undisclosed minority stake as the firm looks to expand its recycling ecosystem and promote responsible waste disposal across India. stories.title: Washington fines 38 companies for plastic recycling failures
stories.summary: The Washington Department of Ecology fined 38 companies a combined $246,548 for failing to meet state requirements for recycled content in single-use plastics. The 2021 law mandates specific levels of recycled material in containers for beverages, cleaning products, and trash bags. Fines ranged from $131 to $43,381.

stories.title: Reconomy opens 20 million pound plastic recycling plant in Corby
stories.summary: International circular economy specialist Reconomy has opened a 138,000 sq ft plastic recycling facility in Corby through its Eurokey brand. The plant is designed to process 38,000 tonnes of material annually. The investment arrives as the UK recycling industry faces competition from cheaper virgin plastics.

stories.title: Constantia Flexibles and NÖM launch paper-based butter wrap
stories.summary: Constantia Flexibles has introduced a paper-based butter wrap in Europe in collaboration with dairy producer NÖM AG. The packaging is designed for recycling in the paper stream. It aims to protect butter from light and oxygen while meeting the specific requirements of the dairy industry.

stories.title: IKEA retailer Ingka Group to invest 1 billion euros in recycling
stories.summary: Ingka Group, the largest global IKEA retailer, plans to invest 1 billion euros into recycling companies to manage waste from discarded furniture and mattresses. The move anticipates European Union legislation that would charge retailers fees for textile waste. Two-thirds of the funding is earmarked for new investments.

stories.title: UK to exempt pub glass bottles from producer recycling fees
stories.summary: The UK government announced plans to exempt glass containers sold to hospitality venues from producer responsibility fees starting April 2027. The change aims to address double-charging for venues that already pay for commercial waste collection. The government is also reviewing how packaging fees reflect recyclability.

stories.title: Roswall confirms single point EPR reporting under Circular Economy Act
stories.summary: Environment minister Romina Pourmokhtari Roswall has confirmed a single point of entry for Extended Producer Responsibility reporting under the Circular Economy Act. The move aims to streamline compliance for businesses operating within the framework. The ministry has yet to detail how the unified portal will function for stakeholders.

stories.title: IIT-D alumnus turns stubble into packaging
stories.summary: Faridabad-based Dharaksha Ecosolutions is using mycelium to convert agricultural stubble into biodegradable packaging. Founded by IIT Delhi alumnus Arpit Dhupar in 2021, the startup aims to address the stubble burning that contributes to severe air quality issues in North India during the winter months.

stories.title: Kraft paper bags face scrutiny as sustainability claims
stories.summary: Retailers are increasingly swapping plastic for kraft paper bags to improve sustainability reporting. While the brown paper aesthetic is popular, experts note that appearance does not confirm recycled content, food safety, or the actual durability of the handles. Sustainability teams are now being asked to document these specifications.

stories.title: Reusable packaging claims require audit
stories.summary: Manufacturers are replacing single-use cardboard with polypropylene honeycomb boards to improve sustainability metrics. While the switch provides clean photographs for reports, auditors are increasingly asking for data on return rates, transport emissions, and the eventual disposal of worn-out trays. The transition is not just visual.

stories.title: SFK Group eyes paper packaging growth
stories.summary: Indian industries are shifting from plastic to paper-based packaging across retail and food sectors. SFK Group CEO Nitin Kaushal says the next phase of adoption depends on improving moisture and grease resistance without sacrificing recyclability. The company is leveraging its background in paper trading to meet this demand.

stories.title: The sustainability paradox in wooden packaging
stories.summary: The wooden packaging sector imports 90 percent of its raw materials despite the country being a leading producer of timber. Businesses are calling for better use of domestic forests to resolve the supply chain disconnect between local production and the downstream manufacturing industry.

stories.title: Heat-seal coatings market forecast to 2035
stories.summary: The global market for heat-seal coatings for paper is entering 2026 with a more regionally diversified supply architecture, according to IndexBox. These coatings are used to enable seals in food and pharmaceutical packaging. The market is expected to see steady growth in demand through 2035.

stories.title: Wet strength additives market grows with tissue demand
stories.summary: The global market for wet strength additives is expanding as manufacturers seek to improve the mechanical integrity of paper exposed to moisture. Demand is tied to hygiene and food service packaging. The sector enters 2026 with more disciplined procurement behavior, according to a new IndexBox report.

stories.title: Paper core label market expands with automation
stories.summary: The market for labels supplied on hollow paper cores is growing as food and beverage companies adopt automated packaging lines. According to IndexBox, the segment enters 2026 with broader demand fundamentals. The industry remains focused on supporting high-speed application across logistics and retail end uses.

stories.title: Review ranks pharmaceutical blister packaging manufacturers
stories.summary: A new market review assesses nine manufacturers of pharmaceutical blister packaging machinery for 2026. The report evaluates equipment capabilities and application contexts. The publisher notes the ranking is based on disclosed criteria rather than market share or performance certification. It is intended for industry buyers.

stories.title: Hosokawa Alpine opens redesigned film test centre
stories.summary: Hosokawa Alpine has opened a redesigned blown film extrusion test centre in Augsburg. The facility allows packaging engineers to test high-output, multi-layer, and orientation technologies under production conditions. The centre debuted during an open house event held on 28 and 29 October 2026.

Polylam Printers invests in digital label press
stories.summary: Greater Noida-based Polylam Printers has acquired an Epson SurePress L-6534VW digital label press. The company says the investment is intended to meet growing demand for short-to-medium-run digital labels. The firm has operated in the printing industry since 1976, starting with a single letterpress machine.

stories.title: Coating head dies market forecast to 2035
stories.summary: The global coating head dies market is entering 2026 with a focus on efficiency and material savings. According to IndexBox, the segment is driven by capital expenditure cycles in flexible packaging and battery production. The market is projected to see continued development through 2035.

stories.title: Corrugated box machine market shifts to automation
stories.summary: The global market for corrugated box making machines is moving toward automated, flexible production lines to meet e-commerce demand. According to IndexBox, the sector enters 2026 with more disciplined procurement behavior. Sustainability mandates are also influencing the design of new production equipment.

stories.title: Foam-in-bag systems market grows with e-commerce
stories.summary: The global foam-in-bag systems market has transitioned from a niche solution to a mainstream packaging method, according to IndexBox. Driven by e-commerce and product safety requirements, the market enters 2026 with a more regionally diversified supply architecture and a focus on on-demand custom cushioning.

stories.title: Coca-Cola warns of pricing pressure from Campa
stories.summary: Coca-Cola has warned that competition from Reliance-owned Campa may force it to cut prices or increase marketing spend to protect market share. The risk was highlighted by Hindustan Coca-Cola Holdings in its draft prospectus for a proposed IPO. Competition is now a formal line item.

stories.summary: The carbonated drinks market in India is seeing intensified competition, and Coca-Cola, the country’s largest cola company, has flagged the same, warning that it may have to cut prices or spend more on marketing to defend its market share against new entrant Campa, the cola brand owned by Reliance Industries.

Gillette India reports 11 percent profit growth
stories.summary: Gillette India reported sales of 846 crore for the quarter ended September 30, a 4 percent increase year-on-year. Profit after tax rose 11 percent to 159 crore. The company cited product innovation and retail execution as drivers, despite facing significant commodity cost pressures during the period.

stories.title: Gillette India reports Q2 sales up 4%, PAT up 11%
stories.summary: Gillette India Limited (GIL) announced its financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026. The company reported a 4% increase in sales, reaching ₹846 crore, and an 11% rise in Profit After Tax (PAT) to ₹159 crore. stories.title: Patanjali Foods profit falls 19 percent
stories.summary: Patanjali Foods reported consolidated revenue of 11,323 crore for the September quarter, a 15.6 percent increase. Net profit fell 18.8 percent to 419.77 crore compared to the same period last year. Higher expenses weighed on the bottom line despite the growth in topline revenue.

stories.title: Hamdard Foods CEO featured in Outlook report
stories.summary: Hamid Ahmed, CEO and Trustee of Hamdard Foods, was named in an Outlook report titled Pillars of Viksit Bharat 2026. The recognition highlights his contributions to the food and beverage sector as part of a mission to transform India into a developed nation by 2047.

stories.title: AMD Industries narrows quarterly loss
stories.summary: AMD Industries reported a standalone net loss of 271.92 lakh for the quarter ended September 30, narrowing from a loss of 294.60 lakh in the same period last year. Standalone revenue from operations rose to 7,852.52 lakh from 5,896.37 lakh in the prior year quarter.

stories.title: Avro India reports quarterly profit of 1.36 crore
stories.summary: Avro India reported consolidated revenue of 29.52 crore for the September quarter, up from 20.90 crore a year earlier. Profit after tax reached 1.36 crore, compared to 1.20 crore in the previous year. The company also reported an operating loss in its plastic waste recycling segment.

stories.title: Anuroop Packaging standalone profit drops
stories.summary: Anuroop Packaging reported a standalone net profit of 2.66 lakh for the September quarter, down from 7.03 lakh in the same period last year. Standalone revenue fell to 14.52 lakh from 77.89 lakh. The company has reclassified assets as held for sale following a decision to divest.

stories.title: Apis India first-half EBITDA rises 55 percent
stories.summary: Apis India reported first-half fiscal 2027 EBITDA of Rs 18.31 crore, a 55 percent increase year on year. Income from operations grew 1 percent to Rs 179.86 crore, while gross margins rose to 46 percent. Honey and dates accounted for the majority of sales. Growth is sweet.

stories.title: Kahan Packaging revenue rises as earnings per share fall
stories.summary: Kahan Packaging reported a 23.3 percent year-on-year revenue increase to 1,841.37 lakh for the first half of fiscal 2027. Net profit rose 6 percent, though basic earnings per share fell to 0.56 from 2.09 following a bonus share allotment. Working capital requirements turned operating cash flow negative.

stories.title: AMD Industries narrows quarterly net loss
stories.summary: AMD Industries reported a standalone net loss of 271.92 lakh for the second quarter of fiscal 2027, narrowing from a 294.60 lakh loss in the same period last year. Revenue rose to 7,552.52 lakh. The company reported a positive standalone net profit for the first half.
